target: Tu la trouves comment ?
english: What do you think of it/her?
tip: trouver here means 'find' in the sense of opinion: Tu la trouves comment? = What do you think of her/it? Literally 'how do you find her?'

target: Tu y crois vraiment ?
english: Do you really believe in it?
tip: 'y' replaces 'à + thing': 'croire à' (believe in) collapses to 'y croire' – 'tu y crois' = do you believe in it.

target: Nous y pensons depuis longtemps.
english: We've been thinking about it for a long time.
tip: depuis + the present tense = have been doing: Nous y pensons depuis longtemps = we've been thinking about it for a long time. French stays in the present.

target: Elle lui a coupé les cheveux.
english: She cut his/her hair.
tip: For body parts French uses 'the' plus an indirect pronoun, not a possessive: lui a coupé les cheveux = cut HIS hair, literally 'cut him the hair'.

target: Veuillez vous asseoir, s'il vous plaît.
english: Please have a seat.
tip: "Veuillez" is the formal imperative of vouloir. Used for polite requests.

target: Il leur a appris a nager.
english: He taught them to swim.
tip: apprendre stacks two à's: à a person, à an action. Il leur a appris à nager = he taught them to swim (leur = à them, à nager = to swim).

target: Tu ne m'en as pas donné.
english: You didn't give me any.
tip: en stands in for 'any/some' of a thing: Tu ne m'en as pas donné = you didn't give me any. English can drop 'any', but French keeps en.

target: Nous lui avons demandé son avis.
english: We asked him/her for his/her opinion.
tip: demander à quelqu'un = ask someone. French asks TO a person, so the pronoun is lui, not le: Nous lui avons demandé son avis.

target: Elle le met dans son sac.
english: She puts it in her bag.
tip: son/sa agree with the thing owned, not the owner: son sac = her (or his) bag, because sac is masculine. The owner's gender is invisible.

target: Je saurai la réponse demain matin.
english: I'll know the answer tomorrow morning.
tip: 'savoir' in the future often means 'find out', not just 'know': 'je saurai la réponse demain' = I'll learn the answer tomorrow.

target: Ils en parlent tout le temps.
english: They talk about it all the time.
tip: parler de something = talk about it, and de + thing collapses to en: Ils en parlent = they talk about it. en sits before the verb.

target: Il m'en a donné un peu.
english: He gave me a little of it.
tip: Me + en: the indirect pronoun comes before en.

target: Parle moins fort, les voisins dorment.
english: Speak more softly, the neighbors are sleeping.
tip: French says 'less loud' for 'more quietly': parle moins fort = speak more softly. fort is the go-to word for volume, not 'loudly'.

target: Tu les attends depuis longtemps ?
english: Have you been waiting for them for long?
tip: attendre already means 'wait FOR' – no preposition follows: Tu les attends = you're waiting for them. Never add 'pour'.

target: Attends jusqu'à ce que le bus arrive.
english: Wait until the bus arrives.
tip: "Jusqu'à ce que" (until) triggers the subjunctive.

target: Tu le retrouves après le travail ?
english: Are you meeting him after work?
tip: retrouver = meet up with someone by arrangement (literally re-find them), not meet for the first time: Tu le retrouves après le travail?

target: Ouvre la fenêtre, il fait chaud ici.
english: Open the window, it's hot in here.
tip: Weather uses faire (to make), not être: il fait chaud = it's hot, literally 'it makes hot'. Same for il fait froid, il fait beau.

target: Rendez-moi ce livre quand vous aurez fini.
english: Return this book to me when you're done.
tip: After quand, French uses the future where English uses the present: quand vous aurez fini = when you're done, literally 'will have finished'. Both actions stay future.

target: N'oublie pas d'acheter du pain en rentrant.
english: Don't forget to buy bread on your way home.
tip: en + the -ant form = 'while/on doing': en rentrant = on your way home, while heading back. French compresses 'while returning' into en + verb.

target: Demain, j'irai au marché acheter des fruits.
english: Tomorrow, I'll go to the market to buy fruit.
tip: To say why you're going somewhere, French just adds a bare infinitive – no 'pour': j'irai au marché acheter des fruits = go to the market to buy fruit.

target: Nous chercherons un hôtel dès notre arrivée.
english: We'll look for a hotel as soon as we arrive.
tip: dès + a noun = 'as soon as': dès notre arrivée = the moment we arrive. Where English needs a whole clause, French uses dès + noun.

target: Elle est triste que vous partiez si tôt.
english: She's sad that you're leaving so early.
tip: Expressions of emotion (triste, content, surpris) + que trigger the subjunctive.

target: Je le vois tous les jours au bureau.
english: I see him every day at the office.
tip: Le is a direct object pronoun replacing a masculine singular noun. It goes before the verb.

target: Nous voulons que vous veniez à notre mariage.
english: We want you to come to our wedding.
tip: French can't say 'want you to come' with an infinitive: 'vouloir que' forces the subjunctive – 'nous voulons que vous veniez'.

target: On va essayer un nouveau restaurant ce soir.
english: We're going to try a new restaurant tonight.
tip: 'aller' + infinitive is the everyday spoken future, like English 'going to': 'on va essayer' = we're going to try. Far more common in speech than 'on essaiera'.

target: Je ne pense pas que ce soit une bonne idée.
english: I don't think it's a good idea.
tip: Negative "penser" triggers the subjunctive. Positive "penser" takes indicative.

target: Nous la lui avons offerte.
english: We gave it (f.) to him/her.
tip: La (fem. direct) + lui. Participle agrees with la (feminine): offerte.

target: Je lui ai prêté ma voiture.
english: I lent him/her my car.
tip: A past participle never agrees with an indirect object: 'lui' sits before the verb, yet 'prêté' stays bare in 'je lui ai prêté ma voiture'.

target: Il faut que tu prennes tes médicaments.
english: You need to take your medication.
tip: 'Il faut que' + subjunctive is the most common subjunctive trigger. 'Prennes' = subjunctive of prendre.

target: Quoi que tu dises, je ne changerai pas d'avis.
english: Whatever you say, I won't change my mind.
tip: "Quoi que" (whatever) triggers the subjunctive.
